meta.what: This file gives the scores of each Earth square of half a degree with at least 15 % bare ground, against each Mars site.
meta.first_pass: This is a first pass. Its squares are 0.5 degree wide, approximately 55 km. On both planets, the heights are 1.85 km apart and each slope covers approximately 3.7 km. The first pass is coarser than the Moon part.
changes: 14 Nov 2026, coordinator's decisions: cold is 0 at +30 C or warmer (it was +15 C), in the yearly and the monthly score
landscape ties are ordered by bare_km2, then by environment, then by id; each place gives squares_with_this_score and each list's tie count is in best_places_tied_at_top
the slope baseline is written 'heights every 1.85 km, slopes across about 3.7 km'; Curiosity's figures are cited as from NASA's public weather feed, which says it is for outreach, not as archive data

sources.data/derived/mars_terrain.json: slopes of the sites and of the Earth squares (agent MARS-TERRAIN): MOLA MEGDR and ETOPO 2022
sources.data/derived/mars_climate.json: Sun, climate and the cannot-match list of the sites; climate and bare ground of the Earth squares (agent MARS-CLIMATE): NASA POWER (MERRA-2), ESA WorldCover 2021, Mars Climate Database, Phoenix MET data from NASA's PDS archive, and Curiosity REMS figures from NASA's public weather feed, which says it is for outreach, not archive data

formulas.terrain: The score is the overlap of the slope histograms of the square and of the site, divided by the overlap of the site with itself. The maximum score is 1.
formulas.dry: The score is 1 at 25 mm of rain and snow a year or less. The score is 0 at 500 mm or more. Between these two points, the score follows a straight line on a log scale.
formulas.cold: The score is 1 if the yearly mean air temperature of the square is equal to that of the site, or colder. The score is 0 at +30 C or warmer. Between these two points, the score follows a straight line.
formulas.bare: The score is the share of the land in the square that is bare.
formulas.sun: The score is the share of the yearly range of noon Sun height at the site that the yearly range of the square covers. Both planets use absolute latitude. The tilt is 25.19 degrees on Mars and 23.44 degrees on Earth.
formulas.landscape: The score is the geometric mean of the terrain and bare scores.
formulas.environment: The score is the geometric mean of the dry, cold and bare scores.
formulas.full: The score is the geometric mean of the terrain, dry, cold, bare and sun scores.
formulas.goal_rule: If a factor is unknown, the goal is unknown. If a factor is 0, the goal is 0.
formulas.month: For each month, the score is the geometric mean of three values. Cold compares the monthly mean air temperature with the yearly mean of the site, on the same scale (0 at +30 C or warmer). Dry uses the precipitation of the month times 12. The third value is 1 if the noon Sun height of the square on the 15th of the month is in the yearly range of the site. If not, it is 0.
formulas.best_months: These are the three months with the highest month scores above 0. The best month is first. Months with equal scores stay in calendar order.

fields.land_share: share of the whole square that is land, from mars_climate.json (WorldCover north of 60 S, Natural Earth south of it); the denominator of bare
fields.bare_km2: bare x land_share x the square's area on a sphere of radius 6,371.0088 km
fields.t2m_year_c: yearly mean air temperature 2 m above the ground, NASA POWER (MERRA-2), C
fields.precip_mm_year: yearly precipitation, rain and snow as water, NASA POWER PRECTOTCORR, mm
fields.pressure_kpa: yearly mean surface pressure, NASA POWER PS, kPa
fields.region / region_group: a plain name from a table of rough boxes in scripts/build_mars_cells.py; group is 'great desert', 'high plateau', 'polar desert' or 'other'
fields.sites.<site>: the five factor scores, the three goals, best_months and falls_short
fields.falls_short.colder_on_mars_by_c: the square's yearly mean air temperature minus the site's, C
fields.falls_short.times_wetter_than_25_mm: the square's yearly precipitation / 25 mm (1 or less: dry enough)
fields.falls_short.pressure_mars_over_square: the site's yearly mean pressure / the square's
fields.best_places.<site>.<goal>: the 10 best squares by that goal, each at least 300 km from those before it, with the month scores; equal scores ordered by bare_km2, then environment, then id for landscape, and by slope_overlap, then id for the other goals
fields.best_places.<site>.<goal>[].squares_with: how many ranked squares have exactly this score (four decimals), this one included
fields.best_places.<site>.<goal>[].bare_km2: the square's bare area, as in cells.<id>.bare_km2
fields.best_places_tied_at_top: per site and goal, how many ranked squares share the list's top score
fields.slope_baseline_km_about: the spacing of the heights (1.85 km); each slope spans two pixels, about 3.7 km (slope_span_km_about)
fields.counts.kept_squares_at_cold_zero_or_warm: ranked squares with a yearly mean of +30 C or more: cold, environment and full are 0
fields.counts.kept_squares_yearly_mean_15c_or_m: ranked squares with a yearly mean of +15 C or more, the first pass's zero point; their cold is no longer 0
fields.climate.citation_note (site cards): how to cite a site's measured figures when they come from NASA's public weather feed; null otherwise

meta.null_rule: unknown is null, never 0; a goal with an unknown factor is null
plan_departures: cells carry region_group, bare_source, elev_mean_m and median_slope_deg besides the job's fields
the cold score uses t2m_year_c, the POWER annual T2M, as MARS-CLIMATE advised
the square's noon Sun height for a month is taken on the 15th of the month
meta.status_caution: NASA does not have a selected site for a human landing on Mars.
meta.climate_caution: Earth climate comes from a grid-box model, not from measurements at each square. The yearly mean temperatures on Mars also come from a model.
validation_caution: This check shows if known analog squares rank higher than control squares.
It does not show that a top square is a better analog than a known site.
Teams selected the known sites partly because they have bare and dry ground. Thus the check against all land is partly circular.
If the check uses only bare squares, the scores do not separate the places that scientists studied from the other squares.
These factors do not measure chemistry, minerals, ice or life. Many coordinates of known sites are estimates.
meta.score_caution: Scores are positions on each factor's scale. They are not shares of likeness to Mars.
meta.intro: This first pass compares Earth squares with Mars sites through the year. It is coarser than the Moon part.
meta.hard_part: The Sun is the easy part for Mars. Cold, dryness, bare ground and landscape are the hard parts.

sites.name: Jezero crater, Perseverance landing site
sites.kind: visited by a NASA mission
sites.why: NASA's Perseverance rover landed here on 18 February 2021, on the floor of a crater that once held a lake and a river delta, and its MEDA station measures the weather at the surface.

sources.what: HiRISE (NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter) image ESP_068360_1985, Perseverance on the ground, 25 February 2021: image centre 18.442 N, 77.452 E
study published in 2023, Nature Geoscience 16, 19-28 (MEDA, first 250 sols): landed at 18.44 N 77.45 E
USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Jezero: crater centre 18.41 N, 77.69 E, 47.52 km across (planetocentric, east, 0-360)

Study published in 2015, abstract 1034, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: the Jezero crater open-basin lake and delta, also proposed as a human exploration zone

sun.how: These values come from a formula that uses the latitude of the site (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees. Over the Mars year, the declination of the Sun changes between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees. Noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|. Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The values are for the centre of the Sun on a flat horizon, without refraction and without terrain. The seasons of Mars are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.093). This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.

sites.name: Gale crater, Curiosity landing site
sites.kind: visited by a NASA mission
sites.why: NASA's Curiosity rover landed here on 6 August 2012, and its REMS station recorded air temperature, ground temperature and pressure on 4,717 sols up to 25 August 2026 while the rover drove uphill from its landing point.

NASA Mars weather feed of Curiosity REMS daily values (Centro de Astrobiologia; marked for outreach use only)

Calef and others 2015, abstract 1020, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: Gale crater (MSL landing ellipse); position as written: Our proposed landing site is located at the center of the final MSL landing ellipse at 137.4019° longitude and -4.5965° latitude (Figure 1).

Study published in 2015, abstract 1022, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: Aeolis Palus, Gale crater; position as written: Latitude and Longitude of the proposed EZ: 4.6°S 137°E

sites.name: Phoenix landing site, northern plains
sites.kind: visited by a NASA mission
sites.why: NASA's Phoenix lander touched down here on 25 May 2008 to test whether water ice lies under a thin soil cover, saw ice in a trench dug by its arm sublimate within days, and its MET station measured the northern summer weather until early November 2008.

NASA/JPL release of 8 February 2021 (SWIM): Phoenix trench Dodo-Goldilocks, ice sublimated over four days

sites.name: Arcadia Planitia (Erebus Montes exploration zone)
sites.kind: studied for a human landing
sites.why: These smooth northern plains possibly hold much water ice in the top metre of the ground. NASA's 2015 workshop studied them as a candidate exploration zone, and NASA's SWIM ice-mapping project names the region for its shallow ice. NASA has not made a decision on a landing site.

sites.name: Deuteronilus Mensae (dichotomy boundary exploration zone)
sites.kind: studied for a human landing
sites.why: Debris aprons are around these mesas. Orbital radar shows that the aprons are mostly water ice under a cover of rock. sun.how: These values come from a formula that uses the latitude of the site (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees. Over the Mars year, the declination of the Sun changes between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees. Noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|. Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.

sun.how: These values come from a formula that uses the latitude of the site (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees. Over the Mars year, the declination of the Sun changes between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees. Noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|. Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The values are for the centre of the Sun on a flat horizon, without refraction and without terrain. The seasons of Mars are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.093). This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.

Over the Mars year, the declination of the Sun changes between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees. Noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|. Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The values are for the centre of the Sun on a flat horizon, without refraction and without terrain. The seasons of Mars are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.093). This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.

Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The values are for the centre of the Sun on a flat horizon, without refraction and without terrain. The seasons of Mars are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.093). This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.

meta.what: Where the known Mars analog sites of data/reference/known_analogs.json come out in the Mars part's scores, and one test of the ranking. A first pass: half-degree squares (about 55 km), heights every 1.85 km, slopes across about 3.7 km.
meta.which_entries: every entry with body 'Mars' or 'both' (the file marks the body in the field 'body': 'Mars', 'Moon' or 'both')
meta.square_rule: the half-degree square that holds the entry's point (twinfinder.mars_climate.square_of); a point on a square edge goes to the square to its north and east
meta.percentile: percent of the kept squares (bare >= 0.15) with a lower goal score, ties counting one half; 100 means no kept square scores higher
meta.rank_among_kept: 1 + the number of kept squares with a higher goal score
meta.scores_outside_kept: a known site whose square has under 15 % bare ground is scored all the same (ranked false); its percentile says where its score would fall

test.how: area under the curve (AUC): the share of (known square, control square) pairs in which the known square scores higher, ties counting one half; 0.5 is no better than chance, 1 means every known square outranks every control
test.known: distinct squares of the Mars and both entries that have climate data; a square holding several entries (such as the Dry Valleys) counts once
test.controls_all_land: the 2000 squares of mars_climate.json (all squares with at least 20 % land) with the lowest sha1 of their id, known squares left out
test.controls_bare: the 2000 kept squares (bare >= 0.15) with the lowest sha1 of their id, known squares left out; tested against the known squares that are kept themselves (an extra, harder test beyond the plan)
test.other_squares_at_the_point: for a point on a square edge or corner, the other squares that touch it, with their goals; not used in the test
test.neighbours_with_data: for a point whose own square has no climate data, the eight squares around it that have; not used in the test
test.unknown: a square with an unknown score is left out of that score's test; the counts say how many remain

previous_cold_zero.what: the same two tests with the first pass's cold scale, 0 at +15 C or warmer, to show what moving the zero point to +30 C did (coordinator's decision of 14 Nov 2026); same known and control squares; not used anywhere else

squares.layout: Columnar little endian. Decode each column as raw / scale; its unknown sentinel means null. A float64 NaN means unknown. A column that has a 'file' field is in that file, at its 'offset' there. A column without a 'file' field is in the file that 'file' of this block names. The columns nearest_site_0 to nearest_site_2 give, for each square, the index in 'sites' of the three Mars sites with the highest score on all factors; nearest_full_0 to nearest_full_2 give those scores.
squares.best_months_rule: A count of zero means no month scored above zero. An unknown count means the months are unknown.
